question: What is the right season window for the White Salmon Glacier route on Shuksan, on foot and on skis?
answer: Two real seasons. SKIS (the dominant use): logged ascents and trip reports run late March through May, April and early May being the sweet spot (stable snow, corn on the way down); January-March outings exist but sit under avalanche terrain (hanging icefall, northwest couloir, wind loading); a late-June ski trip found about 2.5 h of alder brush and broken-up glaciers and advised going earlier. ON FOOT: the approach is a clearcut/slide-alder bushwhack that is only pleasant with snow cover; the glacier itself is snow-only and bridged through July and early August (park-service logs: few open crevasses, steps on Winnie's Slide on July 20 2024), then crevasses open widely on the Upper Curtis and Sulphide glaciers by mid-August and blue ice forms on Winnie's Slide from mid-August into September. The stored Jun-Sep ignores the ski season entirely and runs a little long at the back end.
recommendation: Change the stored season to 'Mar-Sep' and put the explanation in best_season (skiers late March-May, best April to early May; walkers July to mid-August; harder after). A foot-only summer report starting from the White Salmon valley was not found (most summer parties use this glacier as the descent after Fisher Chimneys), so the foot window is inferred from the park-service conditions logs - medium confidence.

proposed.best_season: Ski ascents run late March through May, best in April and early May when the snow is stable and softens to corn. On foot, July through mid-August is the usual window, while the glaciers are still snow-covered and bridged. From mid-August into September crevasses open wide and Winnie's Slide turns to bare ice.
